haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. No counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: 100 requests per minute in total, since all keys of one customer share one budget (Standard plan).
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request never increments the counter, so it uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count goes up before forwarding, so the backend's 500 still uses budget, and the response carries X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded anyway, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and the response has no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: unlimited in v1, until ENTERPRISE_LIMIT_PER_MIN is set.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis in the gateway's region, under key rl-customerId-windowIndex. The key expires when its window ends, removing old counts.
haiku-low.q9: At the start of each fixed one-minute window (:00). The window's key expires at its end, so the count restarts at zero.
haiku-low.q10: Each check is one Lua script on one key, so the read, compare and increment run as one atomic Redis step.
haiku-low.q11: It is the PTTL of the counter key in Redis, rounded up to whole seconds, minimum 1. If not positive, Retry-After is 60.
haiku-low.q12: It does not retry within that request. Each new request tries the store again, with no circuit breaker. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. No counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Standard: 100 requests per minute in total, since all keys of one customer share one budget (counter key uses customer ID). Enterprise: not limited in v1.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After (may also carry X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0). The request is not forwarded; the backend never sees it.
sonnet.q4: No. A denied request never increments the counter, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is incremented before forwarding, so a backend 500 still counts. The client gets the backend response with X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it stops waiting, ignores any late reply, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, forwards the request, and returns the backend's response with no X-RateLimit headers. The request may still be counted if the script ran on Redis.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 per minute. Enterprise: undecided/unset (ENTERPRISE_LIMIT_PER_MIN), so unlimited in v1.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis (counter store), in a counter key rl-customerId-windowIndex holding one integer. Old counts are removed by key expiry: the script sets PEXPIRE to the ms until the window ends on the first increment, so the key disappears when its window ends.
sonnet.q9: Fixed one-minute windows: a new window has a new counter key (new windowIndex), so the count starts fresh at the next minute boundary, and the old key expires when its window ends.
sonnet.q10: Each check is a single Lua script (EVAL) on one key in Redis, so the read, compare, and increment run as one atomic step with no other command in the middle; instances cannot race past the limit.
sonnet.q11: From the PTTL of the counter key (time until the current window ends), rounded up to whole seconds, minimum 1. If PTTL is not positive, the gateway sends Retry-After: 60.
sonnet.q12: Yes, there is no circuit breaker in v1; each request tries the store again (waiting up to 50 ms each). The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, only the backend response.
